chunks: When the sun rises over Mount Thabir and the camels see the places of their hoofprints, then depart. Beware of departing from it before sunrise, lest the blood-offering of a sheep become obligatory upon you. Depart with tranquility and dignity, and be moderate in your walking if you are on foot, and in your movement if you are riding. Hold fast to seeking forgiveness, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
Then depart from where the people depart and seek forgiveness from Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, All-Merciful.
Remaining at al-Mash'ar after the departure is disliked.

When you come to Wadi Muhassir—and it is a great valley between Jam' and Mina, and it is the one nearer to Mina—hasten through it the measure of one hundred steps; and if you are riding, then move your mount a little, and say:
My Lord, forgive, have mercy, and overlook that which You know. Indeed, You are the Mightiest, the Most Generous.
As you said in the mas'a at Makkah. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would move his she-camel in it and say:
O Allah, safeguard my covenant, accept my repentance, answer my supplication, and succeed me concerning those whom I have left behind after me.
Whoever omits the hastening in Wadi Muhassir must return until he hastens through it. So whoever does not know its location should ask the people about it; then proceed to Mina.

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings and supplications for departing from al-Mash'ar al-Haram and passing through Wadi Muhassir during hajj?
ai.summary: This passage outlines the rulings and etiquette of departing from al-Mash'ar al-Haram during hajj, including the prohibition of leaving before sunrise and the recommendation of tranquility, moderation, and seeking forgiveness. It also describes the practice in Wadi Muhassir, including hastening through it and reciting specific supplications, while citing the Qur'anic command to depart and seek Allah's forgiveness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
RETURNING FROM AL-MASH'AR AL-HARAM
When the sun rises over Mount Thabeer and the camels see the ground beneath their feet, begin your departure (ifadah) from Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram. Do not leave before sunrise, as this requires offering the sacrifice of a sheep. As you move, maintain calmness and dignity. Walk deliberately if you are on foot, and proceed with moderation if you are riding. Engage in constant supplication and seek forgiveness, for Allah (swt) says: 
"Then depart from where the people depart and ask forgiveness of Allah (swt). Indeed, Allah (swt) is Forgiving and Merciful." [Surah Al-Baqarah 2:199].
It is discouraged to linger at Al-Mash'ar after the time of departure.
When you reach Wadi Muhassar—a significant valley located between Al-Mash'ar and Mina, closer to Mina—hasten your steps through it for about 100 paces if you are walking. If you are riding, quicken your mount slightly. While passing through, say:
"O Lord (azj), forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know. You are the Most Mighty, the Most Generous."
This is similar to what you say during the sa'i in Makkah. The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, would quicken his camel through this valley while supplicating:
"O Allah (swt), safeguard my commitment, accept my repentance, answer my supplication, and take care of those I left behind."
If you neglect to hasten through Wadi Muhassar, you must return to do so. For those who do not know the location of the valley, they should ask others to guide them to it. After crossing Wadi Muhassar, continue toward Mina.
